title: Senate Banking Chair Summons Ex-Nvidia Chief and Commerce Secretary Over China Espionage Fears
snippet: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has called on former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify following security concerns surrounding Chinese trade oversight and espionage allegations.
content:
WASHINGTON — Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott is demanding answers from former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, calling on both figures to testify before Congress amid heightened national security concerns involving China.

Scott (R-S.C.) confirmed on social media that he has formally requested their appearance before the committee. He emphasized that he would consider issuing subpoenas if Huang fails to testify voluntarily, declaring, "The American people deserve answers."

National Security Scandals and Resignation

The push for congressional testimony comes shortly after Huang stepped down from his post at Nvidia, a company that has served as a primary engine of the global artificial intelligence boom. Huang’s abrupt departure followed reports of his romantic connection with Alice Huang, a businesswoman suspected by U.S. authorities of spying on behalf of the Chinese government.

China has denied allegations that Alice Huang is an operative. Attorney General Todd Blanche stated Thursday that the Justice Department has not reached a definitive conclusion regarding the espionage claims. Neither Alice Huang nor representatives for Jensen Huang could be reached for immediate comment.

Commerce Department Under Scrutiny

Meanwhile, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces mounting pressure from Capitol Hill over the administration's regulatory posture toward Beijing. Lawmakers have criticized Lutnick over the Commerce Department's decision not to place dozens of Chinese firms on the U.S. trade blacklist, as well as questions regarding whether officials adequately monitored Nvidia's technology exports to China.

Tensions surrounding Lutnick have reportedly reached the highest levels of the executive branch. According to two sources familiar with the discussions, senior White House officials are privately debating whether to oust the Commerce chief as concern grows across Washington.

House Committees Escalate Inquiries

The Senate action coincides with an aggressive, parallel investigation in the House. Three key committee leaders — House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast, House China Select Committee Chair John Moolenaar, and House Intelligence Committee Chair Rick Crawford — issued joint demands to Nvidia leadership.

The House panel chairs summoned Jensen Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter to appear for closed-door transcribed interviews scheduled for early December. Lawmakers warned that refusal to comply would prompt subpoenas to force their testimony.

"There are clear national security concerns that need to be addressed immediately," the House chairs wrote in a shared statement, while also summoning Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler for a public hearing on December 3.
